problem: Vision-language models generate object hallucinations in image descriptions, and existing detection methods relying on attention weights fail due to confounders like token position and object repetition.
approach: HaloProbe uses a Bayesian framework that factorizes external description statistics and internal decoding signals to estimate token-level hallucination probabilities, combined with balanced training and a learned prior.
contribution: HaloProbe-guided decoding reduces hallucinations more effectively than state-of-the-art intervention-based methods while preserving caption utility and linguistic fluency.

problem: Existing theory focuses on convergence under heavy-tailed gradient noise but lacks analysis for generalization bounds in this setting.
approach: Develops a general framework using truncation arguments to establish generalization bounds under heavy-tailed noise with bounded p-th centered moment assumption.
contribution: Provides stability and generalization analysis for clipped and normalized stochastic gradient descent and their variants under heavy-tailed noise.

problem: Training recurrent neural networks on long sequences is inefficient due to vanishing/exploding gradients and linear memory scaling in backpropagation through time.
approach: COLA leverages criticality-driven online local alignment using spatiotemporal correlations in the critical regime to enable local learning rules that approximate global error propagation.
contribution: COLA requires only O(H) auxiliary state independent of sequence length and matches BPTT performance on benchmarks while showing superior robustness on stability-sensitive tasks.

problem: Long-tailed multi-label text classification fails because frequent labels form dominant coalitions that suppress rare label learning via superficial shortcuts.
approach: NBCG reformulates multi-label learning as a cooperative bargaining game using Neural Structural Equation Models to identify causal label coalitions and Nash bargaining for credit allocation.
contribution: NBCG adaptively prioritizes under-served label coalitions while maintaining Pareto-efficient trade-offs among all players, improving generalization under distribution shifts.

problem: Computing constrained maximum a posteriori predictions subject to non-convex algebraic constraints remains challenging when neither constraints nor densities are convex.
approach: Proposes a scalable message-passing algorithm for tractable fragments and a general strategy interleaving domain partitioning into convex regions with numerical constrained optimization.
contribution: Structure-aware approach outperforms constraint-agnostic baselines on synthetic and real-world benchmarks for constrained MAP inference.

problem: Differentiable optimization layers rely on expensive Hessian computation via implicit differentiation, limiting scalability and efficiency.
approach: Formulates differentiable optimization as bilevel optimization with a novel active-set Lagrangian proxy to compute epsilon-approximate hypergradients using near-constant first-order information.
contribution: FFOLayer achieves O(log(1/epsilon)) first-order complexity for hypergradient computation and improves overall gradient complexity for constrained bilevel optimization.

problem: In-context learning under strict token budgets is unreliable because models cannot distinguish task-relevant demonstrations from noisy, redundant, or conflicting ones.
approach: RDCO scores demonstrations by marginal task information per token, penalizes redundancy and prefix-conditioned conflicts, and compacts context under bounded divergence constraint.
contribution: RDCO improves 10-dataset classification average by 2.20 points and generation by 2.26 points under the same token budget.

problem: Score-based generative models cannot incorporate probabilistic constraints like fairness or class-level requirements during sampling.
approach: DualScore parameterizes the dual variable of constrained KL-minimization with a neural network to derive an additive score function correction that satisfies constraints.
contribution: DualScore enables constraint satisfaction in pretrained image diffusion models without retraining, demonstrated on fairness and regularized maximum likelihood estimation.

problem: Meta-learning for black-box optimization generalizes poorly on unseen objective landscapes because learnable optimizers never see advanced optimization strategies during training.
approach: MetaDistill uses pretraining on expert optimization trajectories for diversity-preserving distillation, then optional self-supervised fine-tuning for warm-start on unseen tasks.
contribution: MetaDistill significantly improves learnable optimizer generalization on BBOB test suite and control tasks compared to standard training paradigms.

problem: Conversational history biases LLM outputs in unpredictable ways, with hallucinations persisting across turns and affecting subsequent responses.
approach: History Echoes analyzes bias from two perspectives: probabilistically via Markov chain consistency, geometrically via hidden representation consistency.
contribution: Reveals that behavioral persistence manifests as a geometric trap where latent space gaps confine the model's trajectory, with strong correlation between probabilistic and geometric measures.

problem: Conformal p-value-based procedures have limited flexibility, and existing p-to-e-value conversions in conformal prediction are not set-preserving and yield conservative prediction sets.
approach: Proposes P2E calibrator converting conformal p-values to e-values while preserving prediction sets and enabling principled e-value merging with randomization techniques.
contribution: P2E calibrator achieves efficient distribution-free uncertainty quantification with 1-alpha coverage guarantee and improves efficiency over standard baselines.

problem: Multimodal reasoning approaches suffer from static visual-to-text conversion that loses fine-grained details or linguistic dominance that weakens visual faithfulness.
approach: CSMR uses a language model to control reasoning by deciding when to invoke an independent visual perception module to acquire task-relevant visual evidence.
contribution: CSMR consistently outperforms baseline methods on multimodal reasoning benchmarks in zero-shot setting with improved accuracy from cognitive scheduling.

problem: Protein fold classification lacks large-scale non-redundant benchmarks, and existing protein representation learning methods require very large models or fail to scale effectively.
approach: Introduces TEDBench benchmark and proposes Masked Invariant Autoencoders using high masking ratio with SE(3)-invariant encoder and lightweight decoder for self-supervised learning.
contribution: MiAE scales well and outperforms supervised counterparts and baselines on TEDBench, establishing a strong recipe for protein fold classification.

problem: Standard self-supervised implicit neural representation for MRI requires time-consuming per-scan optimization, hindering clinical deployment.
approach: IPOD uses reference-free meta-learning to learn generalized parameter initializations from undersampled data with inverse-problem-driven objective and adaptive meta-update strategy.
contribution: IPOD eliminates dependence on reference images and enables rapid adaptation achieving high-fidelity MRI reconstruction across imaging protocols.

problem: Multimodal large language models perform text-centric reasoning and fail to visualize or track intermediate visual states during complex vision-centric reasoning tasks.
approach: DiffThinker reformulates multimodal reasoning as generative image-to-image task using diffusion model whose denoising trajectory naturally serves as visual reasoning path.
contribution: DiffThinker outperforms GPT-5 by 314.2% and Gemini-3-Flash by 111.6% on vision-centric tasks demonstrating efficiency, controllability, and native parallelism.

problem: Sentence-level watermarking methods remain vulnerable to structural perturbations like sentence splitting and merging from strong paraphrasers.
approach: AliMark reformulates watermarking as bit sequence encoding and alignment problem with two-stage detection using multiple restructured text variants and adaptive alignment.
contribution: AliMark substantially outperforms state-of-the-art baselines under diverse paraphrasing attacks including DIPPER and GPT-3.5.

problem: Conditioned sequence models treat return-to-go as simple numerical inputs rather than aligning them with actual policy performance, breaking their control signal.
approach: Q-ALIGN DT enforces alignment by ensuring Q-value consistency with input return-to-go, using Q-function guidance and RTG-perturbation fine-tuning.
contribution: Q-ALIGN DT achieves superior controllability and performance across D4RL benchmark and generalizes to velocity-tracking where prior methods fail.

problem: Video reasoning models generate textual traces without indicating when and where key evidence appears, making reasoning non-traceable and non-verifiable.
approach: Open-o3-Video integrates explicit spatio-temporal evidence by highlighting timestamps, objects, and bounding boxes with cold-start reinforcement learning using specialized rewards.
contribution: Open-o3-Video improves mAM by 14.4% and mLGM by 24.2% over baseline on V-STAR benchmark with grounded reasoning traces supporting confidence-aware test-time scaling.

problem: Analog circuit verification is bottlenecked by manual interpretation of unstructured specifications, and LLMs struggle with semantic dispersion and numerical precision required.
approach: AnalogVerifier uses neuro-symbolic framework with context-aware task serialization, graph-symbolic scheduling via Port Dependency Graphs, numerical-symbolic grounding, and closed-loop repair.
contribution: AnalogVerifier achieves 82.3%-100% functional pass rate on five industrial analog circuits, establishing new paradigm for end-to-end testbench generation.

problem: Early-exit neural networks rely on calibration for confidence-based exiting, but calibration alone is insufficient for exploiting adaptive computation.
approach: Early-Exit Failure Prediction accounts for both prediction correctness and computation cost, providing lightweight procedure to improve intermediate classifiers.
contribution: EEFP achieves superior cost-accuracy trade-offs compared to calibration and more reliably reflects overall EENN performance.

problem: Mixture-of-Experts routing uses shallow linear projections with limited input structure awareness, leading to unstable and ineffective expert specialization.
approach: STAR augments learnable routing with evolving principal subspace tracking dominant input structure via Generalized Hebbian Algorithm for structure-aware routing.
contribution: STAR consistently improves routing quality and downstream performance on large-scale language and vision tasks with optional test-time subspace updates for robustness.

problem: Global representation steering assumes homogeneous concept representation across embedding space, but LLM representations exhibit clustered, context-dependent structure.
approach: CHaRS uses optimal transport theory modeling representations as Gaussian mixture models, formulating steering as discrete OT problem between semantic clusters.
contribution: CHaRS yields more effective behavioral control than global steering through input-dependent cluster-level shifts via barycentric projection.

problem: Existing benchmarks for multi-agent reasoning and theory of mind in LLMs suffer from narrow scope, data leakage, saturation, and lack interactivity.
approach: Decrypto is a game-based benchmark drawing inspiration from cognitive science and multi-agent RL, designed to isolate ToM evaluation in interactive settings.
contribution: LLMs lag behind humans on key game metrics, and reasoning models are significantly worse at ToM tasks than older counterparts, revealing critical gaps.

problem: Existing cybersecurity evaluations of AI systems are limited in scale and fail to capture the end-to-end lifecycle of vulnerability discovery, PoC generation, and patching.
approach: CyberGym-E2E uses automated agent-enhanced pipeline to transform open-source vulnerability data into realistic evaluation environments at scale.
contribution: CyberGym-E2E provides large-scale benchmark of 920 real-world vulnerabilities across 139 projects for comprehensive evaluation of AI agents' cybersecurity capabilities.

problem: Contaminated reasoning in LLMs from data leakage remains poorly understood, making it hard to distinguish generalization from memorization.
approach: Identifies mutual information decay between representations and gradients as distinctive signal; mechanistic analysis reveals eigenspectrum concentration causing narrowing geometry.
contribution: Demonstrates that narrowing geometry manifests as low-dimensional computation regime, and recovery approach achieves up to 11.03% absolute improvement in consistency.

problem: Recommender systems deployed with fixed parameters degrade over time as user behavior evolves, and formal guarantees are difficult to provide.
approach: CARE wraps arbitrary backbone with adaptive calibration using loss-based monitoring for behavioral change detection and online aggregation with reweighting.
contribution: CARE improves robustness and maintains compact recommendation sets while preserving finite-sample performance guarantees on utility-based risk control.

problem: Deep learning optimization assumes smooth loss landscapes, but modern architectures with ReLU and quantization violate this, causing gradient chattering in adaptive optimizers.
approach: S-Adam introduces Local Geometric Instability metric to estimate Clarke subdifferential diameter, incorporating adaptive damping exp(-lambda rho_t) based on local instability.
contribution: S-Adam achieves convergence to Clarke stationary points at optimal O(1/sqrt(T)) rate with accuracy gains of 6% on CIFAR-100 and 3% on TinyImageNet.

problem: Maintaining indirect reciprocity among decentralized self-interested LLM agents without reliable reputation systems is challenging.
approach: ALIGN enables reputation formation and trustworthiness evaluation through strategically shared open-ended gossip with hierarchical tones, identifying and ostracizing defectors.
contribution: Stronger reasoning capabilities lead to incentive-aligned cooperation, with ALIGN improving indirect reciprocity and resisting malicious entrants.

problem: Training search-integrated reasoning agents via RL is hindered by multi-scale credit assignment problem where sparse rewards fail to distinguish quality reasoning from lucky guesses.
approach: Search-R2 decomposes generation into Actor producing trajectories and Meta-Refiner selectively diagnosing/repairing flawed steps with cut-and-regenerate mechanism.
contribution: Search-R2 outperforms RAG and RL baselines across QA datasets with superior reasoning accuracy and minimal overhead through hybrid reward design.

problem: Single-stream autoregressive interfaces couple state updates with public commitments creating silence tax, and naive early streaming risks premature commitments.
approach: Side-by-Side Interleaved Reasoning makes disclosure timing controllable by interleaving partial disclosures with private reasoning, releasing only supported content.
contribution: SxS improves accuracy-content-latency Pareto trade-offs on AIME25 and GPQA-Diamond across Qwen3 architectures through learned disclosure pacing.

problem: Long-context understanding is limited by context windows, and extending windows indefinitely is impractical.
approach: LIFT stores and absorbs long input information in parameters via dynamic fine-tuning with LLM-generated synthetic tasks, reducing context window requirements.
contribution: LIFT enables short-context LLMs to answer questions requiring information outside inference context with Time to First Token under 10 seconds for 8k inputs.

problem: Constraint-based causal discovery is computationally expensive in high dimensions, and existing divide-and-conquer frameworks assume no latent variables.
approach: DiCoLa extends divide-and-conquer to settings with latent variables by recursively decomposing into subproblems and reconstructing global structure.
contribution: DiCoLa significantly improves computational efficiency across causal discovery algorithms while maintaining soundness and completeness.

problem: Counterfactual identification from counterfactual data remains unexplored since physically realizable counterfactual data was previously unavailable.
approach: Develops ctfIDu+ algorithm for identifying counterfactual queries from arbitrary Layer 3 data, establishing completeness and fundamental limits for non-parametric causal inference.
contribution: Proves which counterfactuals are identifiable from realizable counterfactual data and derives tighter analytic bounds for non-identifiable quantities.

problem: LLMs struggle to bridge theoretical reasoning with verifiable physical simulation and lack runtime perception for transient anomalies.
approach: EmbodiedAct transforms scientific software into active embodied agents by grounding LLMs with tight perception-execution loop and embodied actions.
contribution: EmbodiedAct achieves superior reliability and stability in long-horizon simulations and enhanced accuracy in scientific modeling tasks.

problem: Detecting AI-generated content requires external embeddings, but LLMs implicitly encode self-recognition signals that could enable attribution without external detectors.
approach: Demonstrates reliable self-recognition by steering internal residual stream with random sparse vector to create detectable fingerprint for LLM attribution.
contribution: Achieves over 98% accuracy on LLM identification across multiple settings while preserving generated text quality without semantic interference.

problem: Theoretical understanding of transformers' ability to learn posterior predictive distributions in-context is lacking despite strong empirical performance.
approach: Shows by construction that transformers can implement gradient descent targeting posterior predictive mean/variance followed by nonlinear mappings for PPD binning.
contribution: Establishes error bounds for approximated PPD and demonstrates key role of normalization and attention depth in extrapolation capabilities.

problem: Existing CAD generation methods separate parametric modeling and B-Rep synthesis, missing the intertwined relationship in modern feature-based CAD systems.
approach: FutureCAD uses LLMs to generate executable CadQuery scripts with text-based B-Rep grounding transformer for selecting geometric primitives, trained via SFT then RL.
contribution: FutureCAD achieves state-of-the-art CAD generation performance on new real-world CAD model dataset.

problem: Multi-source reasoning alignment in non-stationary environments transmits systematic biases as source model reasoning distributions evolve unpredictably.
approach: APO formulates alignment as constraint satisfaction under concept drift, treating inter-model divergences as dynamic negative constraints optimized via Plackett-Luce objective.
contribution: APO achieves superior robustness with 7B model outperforming proprietary source models on chest X-ray interpretation with released CXR-MAX benchmark.

problem: Existing world models ignore smooth time-parameterized symmetries in sensory streams, making partial observability prediction unstable over long horizons.
approach: Flow Equivariant World Modeling leverages time-parameterized symmetries within latent memory that shifts equivariantly with self-motion and object motion.
contribution: Framework outperforms state-of-the-art diffusion and recurrent architectures on partially observed 2D and 3D video world modeling benchmarks.

problem: Reinforcement learning with partial observability lacks frameworks when full state observations occur stochastically dependent on the action chosen.
approach: ATST-MDPs introduce action-triggered sporadic observations with Bellman equations and optimal policy existence; under linear MDP, commits to action-sequences between observations.
contribution: Derives ATST-LSVI-UCB achieving regret O-tilde(sqrt(K d^3 (1-gamma)^-3)) matching the known rate for linear MDPs with full observability.
